title: Group Wisdom The Instantaneous and Anonymous Feedback From the Team
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece introduces a facilitation exercise called 'Group Wisdom,' which uses anonymous polling software during a live meeting to collect candid team sentiment on statements about culture, vision, and leadership. It argues leaders avoid this kind of honest, in-the-room feedback because it can turn ugly, yet also need it more than annual engagement surveys provide. The essay walks through the mechanics — QR-code polling tools like Kahoot, Slido, Mentimeter, or MeetingPulse, a Likert-scale warm-up question, then 15 or so substantive statements — and offers a full sample list of statements leaders could use to probe culture, transparency, and meritocracy.
points: Introduces 'Group Wisdom' as a named, repeatable exercise for collecting anonymous, real-time team sentiment during live meetings.
Argues anonymous instant polling surfaces more honest feedback than annual engagement surveys or open group discussion.
Names specific accessible tools (Kahoot, Slido, Mentimeter, MeetingPulse) that make the exercise logistically easy to run.
Recommends starting with a low-stakes warm-up statement before moving into substantive culture and leadership questions.
Provides a ready-to-use bank of roughly a dozen candidate statements covering vision clarity, meritocracy, bureaucracy, and transparency.
quotes: Teams don’t get better unless they can be honest about their strengths and weaknesses during group dialogues. Waiting for the results of the annual enterprise engagement survey often misses the opportunity and the need teams have to hash out what to do differently right now.

One way to ascertain this insight is through an exercise we call Group Wisdom. In this exercise, a leader poses a handful of statements and asks everyone to offer their honest belief about them anonymously.
Because the software does not allow anyone to be identified, the results and individual viewpoints are anonymous and highly candid.

The Group Wisdom exercise commonly involves up to 15 statements and takes about 30-45 minutes to run. Software by Kahoot, Slido, Mentimeter, and MeetingPulse are just a few of the many options available to leaders and facilitators.
Group Wisdom can be an eye-opening exercise for everyone involved and works well even in the largest groups. Consider what an honest snapshot would do for your team.
